title: He Presented My Idea As His Own. He Couldn't Answer One Question.
script: I spent three weeks building a pitch deck for a client renewal, color-coded slides, backup data, the works. The morning of the meeting, my coworker grabbed my files off the shared drive and opened the deck under his own name before I even walked in. He presented it line by line, confident, smiling, taking full credit while I sat in the back row. Then the client asked a follow-up about the churn model on slide nine. He froze. I had built that slide from a dataset only I could access, and he had never actually opened the methodology tab. Thirty seconds of dead silence later, I raised my hand and answered it in under a minute, citing the exact spreadsheet. The client thanked me by name. My manager pulled him aside after the meeting, and within the week the account was reassigned to me, full credit, full commission.
